info.title: Token handler
info.description: Token handler pattern as a service. This service provides authentication and a proxy to other services. Most endpoints are not RESTful, and OpenAPI docs are for reference only.

get.description:
Retrieves the clients available to the tenant, including the clients of the core configuration that are available to all tenants, with their registration status.

Requires the token-handler-admin role. The caller acts on the tenant of their bearer token, which must be from a tenant realm.

parameters.name: core
parameters.description: Set to true to only retrieve the clients of the core configuration.

get.description:
Retrieves an authentication client and its registration.

Requires the token-handler-admin role. The caller acts on the tenant of their bearer token, which must be from a tenant realm. The client is looked up before the role is checked, so an unknown client responds 404 for any caller.

post.description:
Registers an authentication client in the tenant's realm in access service. If provided, the authCallbackUrl is registered with access service as a valid redirect URI, together with the redirectUris of the client configuration, and is not stored in the token handler configuration. Otherwise the client is registered with only the configured redirectUris, and more can be added directly in access service. Registering a client that is already registered replaces its registration; the previously registered client in access service is deleted, including any redirect URIs configured on it. Sends the client-registered event.

Requires the token-handler-admin role. The caller acts on the tenant of their bearer token, which must be from a tenant realm.

registrationToken.description: Initial access token for client registration, from the tenant realm in access service.

authCallbackUrl.description: Optional http or https callback URL to register with access service as a valid redirect URI. Add redirect URIs for additional environments directly in access service after registration.

400.description: Request is invalid, for example a parameter failed validation, or access service rejected the registration token.

example.errorMessage: Registration request failed. Verify registration token.

put.description:
Updates the registered redirect URIs for the authentication client in access service, replacing the current ones. Uses the stored management token from the registration; no external token is required. Sends the client-registered event.

Requires the token-handler-admin role. The caller acts on the tenant of their bearer token, which must be from a tenant realm.

redirectUris.description: List of http or https redirect URIs to register with access service.

400.description: Request is invalid, for example a parameter failed validation, the client is not registered, or access service rejected the stored registration token.

parameters.name: tenant
parameters.description: Name or URN of the tenant. The tenant is kept in the session for the callback. Required unless the X-ADSP-TENANT header is provided, which is used instead if both are provided.

parameters.name: callbackUrl
parameters.description: http or https URL of the callback of the application, which is a valid redirect URI of the client in access service. Required unless the client has the deprecated authCallbackUrl configuration.

get.description:
Initiates sign in via the client by redirecting the browser to the access service authorization endpoint of the tenant's realm. This is a browser navigation, not an API call.

Anonymous: no bearer token or role is required. The tenant comes from the X-ADSP-TENANT header or the tenant query parameter, and the client must be registered for that tenant.

302.description: Redirect to the access service authorization endpoint to sign in.

Location.description: URL of the access service authorization endpoint.

400.description: Request is invalid, for example a parameter failed validation, no tenant is provided, no callbackUrl is provided for a client without authCallbackUrl, or the client is not registered for the tenant.

example.errorMessage: Tenant identity is required in the x-adsp-tenant header or the tenant query parameter.

404.description: The tenant or the client is not found.

example.errorMessage: tenant with ID 'my-tenant' could not be found.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: State from access service, which must match the state of the sign in started on the same session.

parameters.name: X-ADSP-TENANT
parameters.description: Name or URN of the tenant. If it is not provided, the tenant that was provided to sign in on the same session is used.

get.description:
Completes sign in via the client. Access service redirects the browser here with the authorization code. On success the token handler starts a session (the adsp_tk_session cookie), sets the XSRF-TOKEN cookie, and redirects to the successRedirectUrl of the client. Otherwise, including when sign in was not started on the same session, the client is not registered, or access service responds with an error, it redirects to the failureRedirectUrl.

Anonymous: no bearer token or role is required. The request must be on the session in which sign in was started.

302.description: Redirect to the successRedirectUrl or the failureRedirectUrl of the client.

Location.description: The successRedirectUrl or the failureRedirectUrl of the client. Both default to the root of the site.

Set-Cookie.description: The adsp_tk_session session cookie and the XSRF-TOKEN cookie, set when sign in succeeds.

400.description: Request is invalid: the client ID failed validation, or no tenant is provided in the X-ADSP-TENANT header or from signing in on the same session.

example.errorMessage: Tenant identity is required in the x-adsp-tenant header, or from signing in on the same session.

404.description: The tenant or the client is not found.

example.errorMessage: client with ID 'my-client' could not be found.

get.description:
Logs the user out by ending their session in the token handler, and redirects to the root of the site. If the client is configured with keycloakLogout, redirects to the access service end session endpoint instead, which ends the user's session there and returns to the root of the site. Requests that another site caused the browser to make (Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site) only end the token handler session.

Requires a signed in user on the session cookie, authenticated by the same client; no role is required.

Location.description: The root of the site, or the access service end session endpoint if the client has keycloakLogout.

400.description: No user is signed in, the user was not authenticated by the client, or the client ID failed validation.

get.description:
Retrieves the session of the signed in user, as an array with one item. Frontend applications use it to find out whether the user is signed in, and who they are.

Requires a signed in user on the session cookie; no role is required. The token-handler-admin role is intended to list all sessions of the user's tenant, but that listing is not currently supported.

parameters.name: targetId
parameters.description: ID of the target of the client that the user signed in with.

parameters.name: targetPath
parameters.description: Request path on the upstream, relative to the base URL of the upstream in the directory service. It can have any number of segments (for example form/v1/forms), which OpenAPI cannot express. Paths with dot segments ('.' or '..') or encoded path separators are rejected as invalid. The query string is passed to the upstream unchanged.

get.description:
Proxies a GET request to the upstream of the target, with the access token of the signed in user as the bearer token. The access token is refreshed if it is about to expire. The session cookie, CSRF token, and tenant headers of the request are not passed on. The upstream determines the response.

Requires a signed in user on the session cookie; the target must be a target of the client that the user signed in with. No token handler role is required; the upstream checks the roles of the user.

200.description: Request completed successfully by the upstream.

401.description: No user is signed in on the session cookie, or the client of the session is no longer registered so the access token cannot be refreshed.

post.description:
Proxies a POST request to the upstream of the target, with the access token of the signed in user as the bearer token. The access token is refreshed if it is about to expire. The session cookie, CSRF token, and tenant headers of the request are not passed on. The upstream determines the response.

Requires a signed in user on the session cookie; the target must be a target of the client that the user signed in with. No token handler role is required; the upstream checks the roles of the user. The X-XSRF-TOKEN header is required.

requestBody.description: Request body for the upstream, passed on unchanged with its content type.

200.description: Request completed successfully by the upstream.

TokenHandlerClientId.name: clientId
TokenHandlerClientId.description: ID of the client, as configured in the token handler configuration of the tenant or the core configuration.

TokenHandlerCsrfToken.name: X-XSRF-TOKEN
TokenHandlerCsrfToken.description: Value of the XSRF-TOKEN cookie that was set when the user signed in. Required for requests other than GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS.

TokenHandlerTenantHeader.name: X-ADSP-TENANT
TokenHandlerTenantHeader.description: Name or URN of the tenant, for example set by the reverse proxy of an application to restrict it to one tenant. The name can be the tenant name as it is (ignoring case) or in kebab-case form, with hyphens in place of spaces.

TokenHandlerBadRequest.description: Request is invalid, for example a path, query, or body parameter failed validation.

example.errorMessage: Validation failed with error(s): id (params) - Invalid value

TokenHandlerClientNotFound.description: No client with the ID is configured for the tenant or in the core configuration.

example.errorMessage: client with ID 'my-client' could not be found.

TokenHandlerForbidden.description: User does not have the token-handler-admin role in the tenant.

example.errorMessage: User Test User (ID: 0a1b2c3d-4e5f-6789-abcd-ef0123456789) not permitted to get clients.

TokenHandlerNoSession.description: No user is signed in on the session cookie.

TokenHandlerTargetBadRequest.description: Request is invalid: the X-XSRF-TOKEN header does not match the session, the target ID failed validation, the request path has dot segments or encoded path separators, or the upstream of the target cannot be resolved by the directory service or is not in the allowed upstream domains.

example.errorMessage: Request must include valid CSRF token.

TokenHandlerTargetNotFound.description: The client that the user signed in with has no target with the ID.

example.errorMessage: target with ID 'form-service' could not be found.

TokenHandlerTargetUpstreamResponse.description: Any other response is the response of the upstream, passed back unchanged except that Set-Cookie, Set-Cookie2, and Clear-Site-Data headers are removed.

TokenHandlerTooManyRequests.description: Sign in, callback, and logout requests are rate limited to 100 requests per 5 minutes for each client IP address. The RateLimit and RateLimit-Policy headers describe the limit.

text/plain.example: Too many requests, please try again later.

TokenHandlerUnauthorized.description: Request does not include a valid bearer token from a tenant realm. Tokens from the core (platform) realm are not accepted.

clientId.description: Client ID of the registered client in access service. Not set if the client is not registered.

authCallbackUrl.description: Deprecated callback URL of the client configuration. Use the callbackUrl query parameter to sign in instead.

successRedirectUrl.description: URL the browser is redirected to after sign in succeeds. Defaults to the root of the site.

failureRedirectUrl.description: URL the browser is redirected to after sign in fails. Defaults to the root of the site.

core.description: Whether the client is from the core configuration, which provides it to all tenants.

idpHint.description: Identity provider hint passed to access service when signing in.

redirectUris.description: Redirect URIs that are registered with access service when the client is registered.

upstream.description: URN of the upstream service or API, resolved by the directory service.

registered.description: Whether the client is registered with access service for the tenant.

clientId.description: Client ID of the registered client in access service. Not set if the client is not registered.

example.name: My application
example.description: Client for the my application frontend.

example.errorMessage: client with ID 'my-client' could not be found.

tenantId.description: URN of the tenant of the user.

id.description: ID of the user in access service.

roles.description: Roles of the user, from the access token. Realm roles are listed by name, and client roles as '<client>:<role>'.

expiry.description: When the session expires, based on the expiry of the refresh token.

authenticatedBy.description: ID of the token handler client that the user signed in with.
